teach.heading: Same market. Different lens.
teach.body: A higher timeframe shows the bigger picture. A lower timeframe shows the smaller details. Beginners get confused when they treat every timeframe like it has the same job. Lower timeframes are not bad — they're just more detailed. The problem is using detail before you understand the bigger picture.
teach.dayliNote: "The 1M can show me the entry, but it does not decide my whole bias. I need the bigger picture first." — Dayli Scott

experience.prompt: You open the 1M first and price looks messy. Do you stay on 1M and keep reacting, or zoom out to understand the bigger picture first?

reinforce.question: Which timeframe is better suited for bigger-picture direction?
Tap the 4H lens — the one showing fewer candles and a clearer overall direction.
The clean beginner flow is bigger picture, then structure, then ___ detail last.
